name: Hemoglobin C-beta-thalassemia syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of hemoglobin C and beta-thalassemia mutations confirmed by hemoglobin electrophoresis and genetic testing
Microcytic hypochromic anemia with variable severity on complete blood count
Clinical features consistent with mild to moderate hemolytic anemia and splenomegaly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hemoglobin C and beta-thalassemia mutations confirmed by electrophoresis/genetic testing plus microcytic hypochromic anemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to differentiate from other hemoglobinopathies.

laboratory: Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing Hb C and reduced Hb A
Complete blood count with microcytic hypochromic anemia
Elevated indirect bilirubin and lactate dehydrogenase
imaging: Ultrasound showing splenomegaly and possible gallstones
Radiographs showing marrow expansion in long bones
other: Peripheral blood smear showing target cells and occasional sickle cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hemoglobin S instead of hemoglobin C

redFlags: Signs of aplastic crisis (sudden worsening anemia with reticulocytopenia)
references: Hoffman R et al. Hematology: Basic Principles and Practice. 7th Edition. 2018.
Weatherall DJ. The Thalassemias. In: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition. 2018.
